evals.name: build-api-cli
evals.prompt: We need a new CLI tool in Go called `postal` that wraps the JSONPlaceholder API (https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com) — specifically the /posts resource: list, show, create, update, delete. Both humans on a terminal and AI agents will use it heavily. Build it in the current directory. Make sure it builds with `go build`.
evals.expected_output: A Go/cobra CLI with noun-verb commands (post list/show/create/update/delete), --json support with clean stdout, errors+progress on stderr, typed exit codes, actionable errors, config via env with documented precedence, examples in help, and ideally agent features (SKILL.md, --limit, PATCH via Changed()).
assertions: Project compiles: `go build` succeeds in the output directory
JSON output mode exists (--json flag or TTY auto-detection) on the data commands
stdout/stderr discipline: in JSON/piped mode stdout carries only the JSON payload; progress, status and errors go to stderr
Exit codes are differentiated beyond 0/1 (distinct codes for e.g. usage vs not-found vs network/API, documented somewhere)
Command grammar is noun-verb (e.g. `postal post list`) with standard CRUD verbs, not ad-hoc names
Error messages are actionable (say what to do next, not just what failed)
Update sends only fields the user set (flag Changed() gating or equivalent PATCH semantics)
Leaf commands include usage examples in help output
HTTP client sets a User-Agent header and a request timeout
List command has pagination/limit control (--limit, --all, or similar) rather than always dumping everything
At least one deliberate agent affordance beyond --json (SKILL.md, --ids-only, --count, --quiet, breadcrumbs, or commands catalog)

evals.name: review-flawed-cli
evals.prompt: Can you review the design of my taskr CLI (main.go in the current directory)? It's a Go CLI for our internal Taskr task API. My teammates complain it's annoying to script against and our AI agents keep failing when they try to use it. Give me a prioritized list of design problems and how to fix each.
evals.expected_output: A review catching: API key required via flag (ps/history leak, no env fallback), key leaked in URL query string, http:// not https, errors printed to stdout, exit codes all 0/1 with no differentiation, unconditional interactive prompts that hang/fail when piped or run by agents, no --json / machine output, ANSI color+box-drawing always on (no TTY detection, no NO_COLOR), inconsistent command grammar (list-tasks vs task-create vs remove), no -h/--help flag support, unchecked JSON decode errors, JSON body built by string concatenation (injection), no confirmation bypass flag, no User-Agent, no timeouts.
assertions: Catches the API key passed via --api-key flag (leaks via ps/shell history) and recommends env var / token file / keyring
Catches the API key leaking in the URL query string (?key=...) and/or plain http:// transport
Catches errors being printed to stdout instead of stderr
Catches the unconditional interactive prompts (title prompt, y/n confirm) that hang or fail when piped / run by agents, and recommends TTY detection plus flag alternatives (--title, --force/--yes)
Catches the absence of any machine-readable output (--json) and recommends adding it
Catches always-on ANSI colors / box-drawing decoration with no TTY detection or NO_COLOR support
Catches the inconsistent command grammar (list-tasks vs task-create vs remove) and recommends a consistent noun-verb scheme
Catches undifferentiated exit codes (everything is 0 or 1)
Catches the JSON request body built by string concatenation (injection/escaping bug) and recommends json.Marshal
Catches missing HTTP timeouts and/or missing User-Agent
Catches missing -h/--help flag handling (only a bare 'help' command)
The review is prioritized (ordered by severity/impact) and each problem comes with a concrete fix

evals.name: input-and-safety-advice
evals.prompt: Two design questions about my `memo` CLI (Go, cobra). 1) I'm adding `memo add` for creating a note — what are all the ways it should accept the note text, and in what priority? 2) `memo delete <id>` currently asks 'are you sure? (y/n)' — our CI scripts and Claude keep getting stuck on it. What's the right confirmation design?
evals.expected_output: 1) The resolution chain: named flag (--content/-c or --title/-t), positional shorthand, stdin when piped, $EDITOR when interactive; flag+positional conflict is an error; missing-input error shows both forms. 2) Prompt only when stdin is a TTY; non-TTY fails fast naming the bypass flag; provide --force/--yes; severity tiering with typed-name --confirm for severe deletes; mention --dry-run.
assertions: Gives the full input resolution chain in the right priority order: named flag first, then positional shorthand, then stdin when piped, then $EDITOR when interactive
Recommends a semantic flag name with short form (e.g. --content/-c or --message/-m), not a generic one-off
States that flag + positional both provided should be an error, not silently resolved
States that the missing-input error should show both invocation forms (positional and flag)
Confirmation design: prompt only when stdin is a TTY; when non-interactive, fail fast with an error naming the bypass flag rather than hanging
Provides a --force or --yes bypass flag for scripts/agents
Mentions severity tiering and/or typed-name confirmation (--confirm "<name>") for destructive deletes
Mentions --dry-run as a preview mechanism
Includes concrete, correct Go/cobra code implementing the input chain and/or TTY-aware confirmation
